QF.id: IV Code of Conduct and Investor Protection_10

question.text: Per the current NISM IV workbook, which instrument is now used to authorize a broker to issue transfer/pledge instructions for settlement or margin purposes, replacing the demat-related settlement function previously performed under a Power of Attorney (PoA)?

answer.text: Power of Attorney (PoA), which continues to be mandatory and unrestricted
Demat Debit and Pledge Instruction (DDPI), used for transfer and pledge instructions for settlement or margin purposes; PoA is no longer executed for those paragraph-specified activities
General Power of Attorney over bank and demat accounts
A blanket trading authorization filed with the exchange

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the current NISM IV workbook (pp.326–328), PoA is optional and was misused for activities beyond the specified SEBI circular scope. The Demat Debit and Pledge Instruction (DDPI) is used for transfer and pledge instructions for settlement or margin purposes; PoA shall no longer be executed for those paragraph-specified activities. The Trap: PoA was never an unrestricted trading authority, and it is not mandatory; treating it as a current settlement-authority tool ignores the DDPI migration. "Blanket trading authorization" and "general PoA over bank accounts" are not supported by the workbook. Cross-Exam Context: NISM Series IV and VII both test the DDPI/PoA distinction.
